text:
maria: quick note - we've noticed small-tenant latency jitter because the continuous coalesce window admits nearly everything. idea: add a lightweight admission gate that routes tiny requests to a low-latency fastpath while still letting mid-size requests use a warmup lane before the regular batcher.
kevin: curious on semantics: gate returns a routing decision only, right? ADMIT_FASTPATH | ADMIT_WARMUP | DEFER_TO_BATCHER? keep the scheduler stateless w.r.t. tenant heuristics?
maria: yes. gate only decides admission. scheduler keeps execution logic. that keeps interfaces clean and testable.
jamal: we should be explicit about criteria. naive token-counts are ok to start, but incorporate deadline-hint and recent KV-cache-hit history. otherwise we might harm throughput by starving larger flows of cache warmups.
erin: propose two-band rules: fastpath for <=32 tokens and deadline-hint <=50ms; warmup for 33..256 tokens or requests flagged as 'warmup-eligible'. both governed by tenant credits to prevent abuse.
maria: rough proto sketch (toy):
```
fastpath:
  max_tokens: 32
  max_reqs_per_tenant_per_min: 100
warmup:
  min_tokens: 33
  max_tokens: 256
  credit_window_s: 10
  credits_per_window: 5
```
credit window lets bursts through but nudges sustained mid-size traffic to the batcher.
kevin: operational questions: how do we expose config? global defaults + tenant-class overrides (free/paid/enterprise), with an opt-in per-tenant toggle for a few SKUs? per-tenant full config is too much surface.
j amal: agreed. keep per-tenant flags small. also require metrics: counters for decisions and encoded reason tags like "over_rate", "deadline_hint", "kv_consideration" so we can debug policy failures.
erin: fallback behavior: if fastpath compute capacity is saturated, downgrade to DEFER_TO_BATCHER automatically. ops-bot should emit saturation alerts so we can scale or reduce fastpath quotas.
ops-bot: alert: pool fastpath utilization 81% on node-pool-a - suggested action: autoscale or reduce fastpath credits (auto-note).
maria: rollout plan: start in sim-mode for 48h across broad traffic (simulate decisions and emit metrics, but always return DEFER_TO_BATCHER). then enable fastpath at 1% of traffic per box, ramp to 10% while measuring 99th tail and KV hit-rate. A/B with some canary tenants.
kevin: sim-mode is essential. increment a telemetry metric "would_fastpath" and annotate traces with decision reason while keeping execution unchanged.
jamal: testing: perf sims that replay last week's traffic to estimate KV-hit delta and microbench for fastpath latency. also smoke-test kill-switch: route all traffic to legacy batcher at the router if something breaks.
erin: compatibility: gate must not alter request semantics or response ordering. it only affects scheduling path. correlate gate decision ID in tracing span for postmortem.
maria: long-term thought: eventually replace deterministic gates with a tiny decision model that predicts impact on tail latency per-tenant. for now, deterministic rules are easier to audit and roll back.
kevin: docs: add an admission API contract page that defines enums, telemetry labels, and allowed config knobs. keep gate logic isolated in a package-level API so different runtimes (hosted/dedicated/private) can reuse it.
jamal: ensure we record per-path histograms: fastpath latency, warmup latency, batcher enqueue-to-start. that'll show whether warmup actually helps or just increases jitter.
ops-bot: note: schedule maintenance job to collect sim-mode traces daily during rollout for the RFC authors.
erin: next steps: maria will draft RFC with proto, enums, telemetry, rollout cadence, and perf-sim plan. kevin/jamal will run initial sims and share CSVs. i'll wire ops-bot alerts to the canary stack.
maria: I'll have the RFC draft and sim-mode data attached by EOD Friday. thanks all. :rocket:
